name: C-EVAL
description: C-EVAL is a comprehensive Chinese evaluation suite designed to assess advanced knowledge and reasoning abilities of foundation models in a Chinese context. It comprises 13,948 multiple-choice questions across 52 diverse disciplines spanning four difficulty levels: middle school, high school, college, and professional. The questions range from humanities to science and engineering.

creator.name: Yuzhen Huang, Yuzhuo Bai, Zhihao Zhu, Junlei Zhang, Jinghan Zhang, Tangjun Su, Junteng Liu, Chuancheng Lv, Yikai Zhang, Jiayi Lei, Yao Fu, Maosong Sun, Junxian He

citeAs: Yuzhen Huang, Yuzhuo Bai, Zhihao Zhu, Junlei Zhang, Jinghan Zhang, Tangjun Su, Junteng Liu, Chuancheng Lv, Yikai Zhang, Jiayi Lei, Yao Fu, Maosong Sun, Junxian He. C-EVAL: A Multi-Level Multi-Discipline Chinese Evaluation Suite for Foundation Models. NeurIPS 2023 Track on Datasets and Benchmarks.
rai:dataCollection: The data is collected from mock exams freely available on the internet, past exam questions from top universities in China publicly shared by students, and mock questions for the national graduate entrance exam from the Weipu website (around 2000 questions with authorization). The questions are collected from four difficulty levels: middle school, high school, college, and professional tests across 52 diverse disciplines.
rai:dataCollectionType: Web Scraping, Secondary Data analysis, Document analysis
rai:dataCollectionRawData: Mock exams from the internet (primarily as PDF or Microsoft Word documents and a minor fraction as web pages), past exam questions from top universities in China, and mock questions for the national graduate entrance exam from the Weipu website.
rai:dataManipulationProtocol: Questions with fewer than four options were eliminated, and incorrect choices were randomly dropped for questions with more than four options to ensure all questions have exactly four choices.
rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: PDF documents were initially processed into text. All questions were parsed (automatically when possible, otherwise manually by the authors) into a structured format. For subjects with complex mathematical notations, manual conversion into standard LaTeX formats was performed. Standard data preprocessing including deduplication and cleaning was applied. Questions underwent several rounds of human validation by the authors, and all LaTeX notations were ensured to compile without syntax errors. At least around 200 questions were processed for each subject, and questions were randomly split into development (5 exemplars per subject), validation, and test sets with a 1:9 ratio for validation and test.
rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Development split exemplars were annotated with explanations to enable few-shot chain-of-thought settings. Explanations were generated by combining automatic generation and human annotation: GPT-4 was prompted to generate step-by-step explanations for ground-truth answers, then the generated explanations were manually revised by the authors to obtain final explanations.
rai:annotationsPerItem: One explanation per development set item (5 exemplars per subject)
rai:annotatorDemographics: The authors (researchers from Shanghai Jiao Tong University, Tsinghua University, University of Edinburgh, and The Hong Kong University of Science and Technology) performed manual annotation and validation.
rai:machineAnnotationTools: GPT-4 was used to generate initial step-by-step explanations for the development split, which were then manually revised.
rai:dataSocialImpact: C-EVAL is designed to evaluate LLMs' capabilities in a Chinese context, assessing knowledge of Chinese users' primary interests such as Chinese culture, history, and laws. The benchmark aims to guide developers in understanding model abilities from multiple dimensions and facilitate the growth of foundation models for Chinese users.
rai:dataLimitations: The benchmark primarily focuses on multiple-choice questions as a proxy for evaluating advanced abilities. While this format provides clearly defined metrics, it may not capture all aspects of LLM capabilities. The authors acknowledge that C-EVAL, along with English-language benchmarks, is far from perfect for LLM evaluation, as there are many other abilities (such as reasoning over and calling APIs) and aspects beyond accuracy (including safety, bias, and robustness) that are not covered. Potential data contamination is a concern, though efforts were made to mitigate this by using mock exams and local exam questions rather than official national exam questions.
rai:dataUseCases: The dataset is intended for evaluating foundation models' advanced knowledge and reasoning abilities in a Chinese context. It can be used for testing and validation purposes. The benchmark includes development, validation, and test splits, where the development split (5 exemplars per subject) facilitates few-shot evaluation, the validation split is intended for hyperparameter tuning, and the test split (with private labels) is used for final evaluation through submission to the website. C-EVAL can be used as a whole or subsets can be separately utilized to assess certain model abilities of interest.
